question: A pregnant farmer asks you if she should stop all physical work. What is your best advice?

options.A: Continue heavy farming work as normal to build endurance
options.B: Switch entirely to night shifts for all physical activities
options.C: Stop working immediately and stay in bed until delivery
options.D: Avoid exhausting labor and heavy lifting while resting often

explanation: Light activity is totally fine and healthy, but heavy lifting and exhausting work can put stress on the pregnancy. Encourage her to listen to her body and rest well. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h2)

question: How should a normal optic disc appear during a fundus examination?

options.A: Sharp, well-defined borders with a creamy pink or yellowish color
options.B: An irregular white scar tissue mass blocking the blood vessels
options.C: Blurred, swollen edges with dark purple patches throughout
options.D: A completely black circle surrounded by bright green rings

explanation: A healthy optic disc has crisp, distinct margins and a distinct yellowish-pink or creamy color without swelling. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h7)

question: What makes a malignant tumor much more dangerous than a benign one?

options.A: Their tendency to cause severe local pain within days of starting
options.B: The fact that they always grow much larger than benign lumps
options.C: The complete absence of blood vessels inside their tissue mass
options.D: The ability to invade nearby structures and spread to distant organs

explanation: Malignant cells are troublemakers because they don't stay put. They love to break away and travel to other parts of the body. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T7#GNS321_U1_T7_h2)

question: For how many months should a baby be exclusively breastfed?

options.A: The first 9 months of life
options.B: The entire first year of life
options.C: The first 6 months of life
options.D: The first 3 months of life

explanation: Correct! Breast milk alone provides all the water, food, and protection a baby needs for their first 6 solid months. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why must a nurse always clean an instrument before disinfecting it?

options.A: To sterilize the equipment without using heat or gas
options.B: To dry the medical instrument so it does not rust
options.C: To remove organic matter that can block chemical disinfectants
options.D: To instantly kill all bacterial spores present on the surface

explanation: Think of dirt or dried blood as a shield for germs! Cleaning washes away that organic barrier so your disinfectant can actually reach and kill the bacteria. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h2)

question: When a baby's head is nicely tucked with the chin to the chest, what is the measurement of the suboccipito-bregmatic diameter?

options.D: 9.5 cm

explanation: When the baby tucks its chin right into its chest, it presents its smallest and best measurement for birth: 9.5 centimeters. Beautiful design by nature! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h3)

question: What does a grassroots approach to community health rely on most?

options.A: Complete reliance on imported foods for malnourished children
options.B: Strict enforcement of police patrols around local markets
options.C: Direct funding and management by foreign governments only
options.D: Active involvement and ownership by local community members

explanation: Grassroots programs succeed by empowering local residents to lead and sustain health initiatives within their own homes and villages. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h8)

question: When would the Ministry of Health use syndromic surveillance?

options.A: When they want to check the exact financial budget of a rural hospital
options.B: When they need the absolute fastest warning about a potential outbreak based on symptoms
options.C: When laboratory tests are cheap and results are ready within minutes
options.D: When they need a complete census of all chronic illnesses

explanation: Syndromic surveillance watches out for symptom groups (like sudden fever and rashes) even before lab results come back, giving us a super-fast early alarm! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h3)

question: Why must a nurse check for a germ or fungus infection before giving a strong steroid eye drop?

options.A: Viral infections always require heavy systemic steroids
options.B: Antifungal drugs neutralize the active ingredients in steroids
options.C: Steroid drops only work if mixed with an antibiotic first
options.D: Steroids weaken the local immune response and can make infections spread

explanation: Steroids calm down inflammation by putting the brakes on the immune system. If a hidden fungus or virus is present, that brake-action lets the germ throw a party and spread! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h4)

question: When is it completely unsafe to give a patient medication by mouth?

options.A: When the drug is manufactured as a small tablet
options.B: When the patient is unconscious or unable to swallow
options.C: When the medication is inexpensive to produce
options.D: When the patient has a mild headache

explanation: Great nursing instinct here! If a patient cannot swallow or is unconscious, giving oral meds puts them at severe risk of choking and getting fluid into their lungs. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T4#GNS125_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is a crucial piece of advice a nurse should give a patient starting daily hormone pills?

options.A: Double your dose whenever you feel stressed or tired
options.B: Never stop taking the medication without consulting your doctor
options.C: Stop the pills once your blood test results return to normal
options.D: Take the medication only when you feel sluggish or dizzy

explanation: Stopping hormone replacement out of nowhere can trigger a life-threatening crisis. Always remind patients to talk to their doctor first! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h8)

question: Why is it so important to involve the community at every single stage of a health program?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for baseline surveys
options.B: It allows the government to avoid paying health workers
options.C: It ensures interventions address real, locally felt needs
options.D: It speeds up the construction of primary health centers

explanation: Spot on! When locals help plan from day one, we make sure we are actually solving the problems they care about most, rather than guessing what they need. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h2)

question: What are the prominent parallel ridges found on the front surface of the medulla called?

options.A: The pyramids
options.B: The olives
options.C: The pons
options.D: The peduncles

explanation: You got it! The pyramids are the distinct ridges on the front (anterior) surface of the medulla that carry important motor pathways down from the brain. Keep building that knowledge! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h2)

question: What is the primary function of bile salts in digestion?

options.A: Digesting proteins
options.B: Emulsifying fats
options.C: Neutralizing stomach acid
options.D: Absorbing carbohydrates

explanation: Bile salts break large fat globules down into smaller droplets through emulsification, giving digestive enzymes more surface area to act upon. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a routine component of a comprehensive clinical assessment for a febrile patient?

options.A: Monitoring respiratory and pulse rates
options.B: Checking the level of consciousness
options.C: Measuring daily bone mineral density
options.D: Observing skin warmth and diaphoresis

explanation: Bone density measurements are unrelated to the acute assessment of a febrile illness. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T6#GNS123_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of evaluating a community health program?

options.A: To punish staff members who failed to meet performance targets
options.B: To determine if the program met its goals and improved health outcomes
options.C: To increase the cost of healthcare services for local residents
options.D: To make sure no documentation paperwork is ever filed twice

explanation: Evaluation lets nurses see if their efforts actually helped the community or if changes are needed. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why is the pelvis of a young adolescent girl usually not ready for childbirth?

options.A: It lacks adequate muscle attachment
options.B: It expands beyond normal size during puberty
options.C: It is still growing and not fully developed
options.D: It calcifies too early in childhood

explanation: An adolescent's pelvis hasn't reached full growth yet, which causes major physical blocks and dangers during delivery. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h3)

question: What exactly is caregiver burnout?

options.A: A state of physical, emotional, and mental exhaustion from long-term caregiving
options.B: A sudden financial profit gained from running a home care agency
options.C: A formal medical diagnosis of dementia given to family members
options.D: A temporary feeling of tiredness after cleaning the house

explanation: Caregiving is heavy work. Burnout happens when looking after a loved one drains all physical and emotional energy without enough rest. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h7)

question: A patient is using their neck and shoulder muscles heavily to take every breath. What does this sign indicate?

options.A: The patient has a normal, healthy breathing pattern
options.B: The patient's lungs are expanding with minimal effort
options.C: The patient is in a deeply relaxed sleeping state
options.D: The patient is experiencing increased respiratory effort and distress

explanation: Using accessory muscles means the main breathing muscles need extra help because breathing has become difficult. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why do community nutrition programs sometimes struggle when they introduce unfamiliar foreign foods?

options.A: Local kitchens are physically unable to cook imported ingredients
options.B: Foreign foods contain no vitamins or minerals whatsoever
options.C: Food is deeply connected to personal identity, comfort, and tradition
options.D: Community members refuse to eat anything that has been grown locally

explanation: Spot on! Food is personal and tied to our comfort and identity. If you ignore local food culture, people naturally won't vibe with it. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T030#GNS227_U2_T030_h6)

question: What is the main job of foetal circulation?

options.A: To supply oxygen and nutrients from the mother
options.B: To pump blood directly into the mother's kidneys
options.C: To circulate air through the baby's developing lungs
options.D: To filter all waste through the baby's own kidneys

explanation: You've got this! Since a baby in the womb cannot breathe air or eat food yet, the placenta steps in to bring oxygen and nutrients straight from the mother's blood. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h1)

question: Which professional is best suited to help community nurses promote backyard farming?

options.A: Hospital biomedical engineer
options.B: Surgical theater technician
options.C: Emergency room pharmacist
options.D: Agricultural extension worker

explanation: Agricultural workers have the expertise in crop growing and farming techniques needed to support backyard gardens. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h7)

question: Why do growing malignant tumors desperately need angiogenesis?

options.A: It supplies necessary oxygen and nutrients while removing metabolic waste
options.B: It provides a hard outer shell that keeps the tumor tightly enclosed
options.C: It protects the tumor cells from being destroyed by radiation therapy
options.D: It prevents white blood cells from attacking the cancerous mass

explanation: Just like us, tumors need food and oxygen to keep growing, plus a way to take out the trash! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T7#GNS321_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the maximum recommended time limit for a single intubation attempt to protect the patient?

options.A: 30 seconds
options.B: 5 minutes
options.C: 2 minutes
options.D: 10 minutes

explanation: Limiting attempts to 30 seconds prevents prolonged interruption of oxygen delivery and avoids severe hypoxia. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why do we generally avoid giving live vaccines to pregnant women?

options.A: Live vaccines deactivate automatically in pregnant bloodstreams
options.B: Hormonal changes turn live viruses into strong bacteria
options.C: Pregnant women always develop permanent immunity instantly
options.D: There is a theoretical risk of harming the developing fetus

explanation: Live vaccines contain weakened germs that might pose risks during pregnancy, so we prefer using safe, inactivated options instead. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h3)

question: When doing a community assessment, what does 'resource mapping' actually involve?

options.A: Counting how many patients die in the regional hospital
options.B: Listing roads that need paving by the federal government
options.C: Identifying local strengths, active groups, and facilities
options.D: Calculating the exact profit of local medicine shops

explanation: Resource mapping is like drawing a treasure map of your community's strengths—finding local groups, clinics, and assets that can help improve health. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h4)

question: A pregnant woman who smokes and drinks alcohol falls under which category of risk?

options.A: Genetic factors
options.B: Anatomical factors
options.C: Lifestyle factors
options.D: Obstetric factors

explanation: Behaviors like smoking and alcohol consumption are classified as lifestyle risk factors that can negatively impact fetal development. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h2)

question: How does the body primarily generate heat when exposed to cold environments?

options.A: By increasing sweat production
options.B: Through muscle activity and shivering
options.C: Through rapid blood vessel expansion
options.D: By decreasing cellular metabolism

explanation: Shivering and physical muscle movement increase cellular work, which quickly generates heat to warm the body. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why are older adult patients at a higher risk for medication mix-ups during home care?

options.A: Their bodies cannot process basic tap water safely
options.B: They frequently take multiple medications at the same time
options.C: They always refuse to take any form of pill or liquid
options.D: Doctors rarely prescribe standard adult doses to seniors

explanation: Taking many drugs at once (polypharmacy) increases the chance of drug interactions, side effects, and confusion. You'll see this often in community health! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why do certain cultural practices place strict food bans on women during pregnancy?

options.A: To prevent birth deformities or ease future labor pains
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of feeding the family
options.C: To comply with international medical guidelines
options.D: To ensure the mother loses weight before delivery

explanation: These bans usually come from a place of protection—people genuinely worry that certain foods might harm the baby or make delivery difficult, even though science says otherwise. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T016#GNS227_U2_T016_h4)

question: What is the real difference between just hearing someone talk and active listening?

options.A: Active listening can only be performed in a quiet hospital office.
options.B: Hearing requires the nurse to offer immediate medical diagnoses.
options.C: Active listening involves full concentration on both words and underlying emotions.
options.D: Hearing requires the nurse to write down every spoken word verbatim.

explanation: Active listening means tuning into the feelings behind the words, not just waiting for your turn to speak. Great nurses master this! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h4)

question: Why might doctors order a thyroid test for a patient with severe hyperemesis?

options.A: It helps check the exact gestational age of the fetus
options.B: Thyroid failure is the primary cause of all pregnancy vomiting
options.C: High levels of hCG can temporarily stimulate the thyroid gland
options.D: Thyroid medication is always used to cure morning sickness

explanation: Because hCG hormone looks a bit like thyroid-stimulating hormone, sky-high pregnancy hormones can trick the thyroid into working overtime. Brilliant clinical insight! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h5)

question: What is a core day-to-day duty of nurses and midwives in Nigerian reproductive health care?

options.A: Providing direct clinical care, health education, and community outreach
options.B: Writing national health insurance laws in the federal legislature
options.C: Manufacturing contraceptive implants in national laboratories
options.D: Importing specialized surgical instruments from overseas

explanation: Exactly! Nurses and midwives are on the frontline, delivering care at the bedside and educating communities on healthy living. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h6)

question: What often causes the biggest hurdles for people with physical disabilities in daily life?

options.A: Inaccessible physical environments and negative social attitudes
options.B: A lack of interest in attending family social gatherings
options.C: The mandatory use of modern assistive walking frames
options.D: Excessive consumption of prescribed rehabilitation vitamins

explanation: Often, bad societal attitudes and buildings without ramps or lifts cause more barriers than the physical condition itself. We must be change agents! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h9)

question: Why must a nursing unit's objectives match the wider hospital vision?

options.A: It ensures every department pulls in the same direction.
options.B: It guarantees an increase in annual government funding.
options.C: It completely removes the need for nursing supervisors.
options.D: It allows nurses to change hospital policies at will.

explanation: When everyone shares the same focus, different departments work together smoothly instead of working against each other. [learn more](GST321_U2_T1#GST321_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common barrier to effective community health data collection in Nigeria?

options.A: An excess of modern computers in every rural primary health clinic
options.B: Too many trained nurses working in remote village settlements
options.C: Inadequate funding, difficult terrain, and security challenges
options.D: Strict laws that ban community surveys across all local governments

explanation: Logistical hurdles, funding shortages, and security risks often complicate health assessments in the field. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h8)

question: What should you do with the AED pads after the patient suddenly regains a pulse and starts breathing?

options.A: Leave the pads attached in case the heart rhythm deteriorates again
options.B: Peel them off immediately to allow the chest skin to breathe
options.C: Move both pads to the patient's back for continuous ECG monitoring
options.D: Disconnect the cable but leave the sticky pads on the skin

explanation: Keep those pads on! Patients who just recovered from cardiac arrest can easily slip right back into a dangerous rhythm. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why do doctors often order a brain scan before doing a lumbar puncture on a suspected meningitis patient?

options.A: To make sure high pressure in the brain won't cause the brainstem to herniate.
options.B: To warm up the lower back before the needle goes in.
options.C: To measure the exact blood flow through the carotid arteries.
options.D: To completely replace the need to test the cerebrospinal fluid.

explanation: Safety first! If there's too much pressure building up inside the head, draining fluid from the lower back can create a dangerous suction effect, pushing the brain downward. A scan checks if it's safe first. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T17#GNS222_U3_T17_h5)

question: What are the standard settings for a hospital autoclave?

options.A: 72 degrees Celsius for 15 seconds
options.B: 100 degrees Celsius at atmospheric pressure
options.C: 160 degrees Celsius with dry heat
options.D: 121 degrees Celsius at 15 psi

explanation: Remember 121 degrees Celsius and 15 pounds of pressure! That magic combo of hot steam kills spores reliably every time. [learn more](GST114_U2_T11#GST114_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why is it super important to make sure the IV line is working well before starting a chemo infusion?

options.A: To prevent severe tissue damage from drug leakage
options.B: To keep the infusion pump from sounding false alarms
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling dizzy during treatment
options.D: To ensure the medication absorbs faster in the stomach

explanation: You nailed it! If chemo leaks outside the vein into the skin, it can destroy the surrounding tissue (called extravasation), so checking the IV is critical. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T7#GNS215_U6_T7_h6)

question: Why is community ownership so important for the long-term success of health projects?

options.A: It guarantees that the clinic will make a profit from drug sales.
options.B: It removes all responsibilities from the shoulders of community nurses.
options.C: Locals will sustain and protect the program after external support ends.
options.D: Government health budgets will no longer be needed at all.

explanation: Exactly! When the community feels the project is theirs, they will keep it running strong long after outsiders pack up and leave. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main job of the trophoblast layer in a developing blastocyst?

options.A: It surrounds the egg to form the protective corona radiata
options.B: It forms the outer layer that assists with implantation and placenta development
options.C: It develops directly into the internal organs of the growing fetus
options.D: It creates the fast block to prevent extra sperm from entering

explanation: You nailed it! The trophoblast acts like a pioneer, helping the embryo burrow into the uterine lining to build a healthy placenta. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T8#GNS121_U5_T8_h7)

question: What HbA1c blood test result is generally used to diagnose diabetes?

options.A: 8.0% or higher
options.B: 10.5% or higher
options.D: 6.5% or higher

explanation: An HbA1c of 6.5% or higher shows that blood sugar has been running high over the past three months. It's a key lab value you'll use all the time in practice! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h5)

question: A PAC patient is stable and ready to go home. What is the best next step for the nurse?

options.A: Provide compassionate contraceptive counseling and discharge instructions
options.B: Withhold discharge until a family elder arrives to sign papers
options.C: Scold the patient so she does not experience complications again
options.D: Prescribe heavy sedatives to prevent emotional processing

explanation: Before they leave, always give clear discharge notes and friendly, non-judgmental advice on how to prevent another unplanned pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h8)

question: How do prospective study findings directly benefit frontline nurses working in clinical wards?

options.A: By providing historical background on ancient medical discoveries
options.B: By eliminating the need for patient assessments during night shifts
options.C: By replacing all bedside charting with automated computer algorithms
options.D: By helping identify high-risk patients early so preventative nursing care can be applied

explanation: Prospective research uncovers risk factors that frontline nurses use to spot vulnerable patients and prevent adverse hospital events. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h7)

question: What does healthcare outsourcing actually mean?

options.A: Hiring external vendors to perform specific hospital operations or services
options.B: Closing down public health clinics to build private pharmacies
options.C: Permanently selling public hospitals to private business owners
options.D: Transferring clinical nurses to foreign healthcare institutions

explanation: Outsourcing is like hiring an outside expert to handle specific tasks (like security or laundry) while the hospital stays in charge of the big picture. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why do patients often feel sudden cramping when the scope enters the sigmoid colon?

options.A: The scope has to poke through the muscular wall.
options.B: The natural S-curves and movement of this bowel make it sensitive to stretching.
options.C: The rectum is completely bypassed.
options.D: Numbing medicine causes muscle spasms.

explanation: Exactly! Navigating those twists and turns stretches the bowel wall a bit, which triggers nerves and causes temporary cramping. Totally normal response! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h2)

question: How does the high humidity inside a steam tent help a patient with a heavy cough?

options.A: It dilates the tiny air sacs in the lower lungs
options.B: It kills bacterial infections in the upper airway
options.C: It numbs the throat nerves to stop the cough reflex
options.D: It liquefies thick mucus so it is easier to clear

explanation: Spot on! Moisture acts like magic on sticky mucus, thinning it out so the patient can cough it up easily. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h1)

question: What term describes the wear and tear on the body from long-term, ongoing stress?

options.A: Systemic exhaustion
options.B: Adverse adaptation
options.C: Allostatic load
options.D: Homeostatic balance

explanation: 'Allostatic load' is just a fancy way of saying your body gets tired and worn down from fighting stress day after day without a break. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T8#GNS123_U1_T8_h6)

question: In healthcare quality improvement, what does "spreading" an idea mean?

options.A: Spreading a contagious disease from one patient room to another
options.B: Expanding the physical size of the hospital emergency department
options.C: Increasing the total number of nursing staff on every hospital shift
options.D: Taking a successful local change and sharing it with other units or facilities

explanation: You've got this! Spread simply means taking a great idea that worked well in one ward and sharing it so other care areas can benefit too. [learn more](GST319_U1_T6#GST319_U1_T6_h1)

question: A patient told you, "The lab definitely mixed up my blood results, I am completely healthy," right after a terminal diagnosis. Which stage of grief is this?

options.A: Bargaining
options.B: Depression
options.C: Denial
options.D: Acceptance

explanation: Rejecting a painful reality is a natural defense mechanism called denial. It helps the mind cope in the early stages of grief. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T6#GNS221_U4_T6_h2)

question: Why does damaged joint cartilage take such a long time to heal?

options.A: It lacks a direct blood supply
options.B: It is constantly dissolved by joint fluid
options.C: It has too many active breakdown cells
options.D: It contains no cells at all

explanation: Because cartilage doesn't have its own blood vessels, healing nutrients have to slowly ooze in from nearby tissues, making repair a very slow process. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T1#GNS222_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a good alternative for severe hot flashes if a patient cannot take hormone therapy?

options.A: High-dose systemic testosterone injections
options.B: Strict fluid restriction during the evening hours
options.C: Low-dose non-hormonal neuromodulators like select SSRIs
options.D: Immediate surgical removal of the adrenal glands

explanation: Certain non-hormonal medications help calm the brain's thermostat to relieve hot flashes safely when hormones aren't an option. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T15#GNS121_U5_T15_h6)

question: What is the main difference between civil liability and criminal liability for a nurse?

options.A: Criminal liability is resolved through financial compensation to the patient.
options.B: Criminal liability addresses offenses against the state punishable by jail or fines.
options.C: Civil liability only applies to doctors, never to registered nurses.
options.D: Civil liability involves state imprisonment while criminal involves apologies.

explanation: Criminal law deals with public safety offences prosecuted by the state (like jail time or fines), whereas civil law is usually about private disputes and compensation. Good to know for practice! [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h4)

question: What is the main reason for teaching pregnant women about pregnancy danger signs right in their homes?

options.A: To frighten them into staying indoors
options.B: To reduce the number of required antenatal visits
options.C: To ensure they recognize complications early and seek prompt help
options.D: To test their memory during clinic visits

explanation: When mums and families know what warning signs look like (like heavy bleeding or severe headaches), they act fast before things get dangerous. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T4#GNS225_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which step of the nursing process involves checking if the patient got better after your advice?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Diagnosis
options.D: Assessment

explanation: You got it! Evaluation is our final check where we look back at our care plan to see if the patient's condition improved and if our goals were met. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h4)

question: What essential document must go with a patient when transferring her from a clinic to a bigger hospital during an emergency?

options.A: A blank sheet of paper for the hospital doctors to sign
options.B: A clear referral note detailing interventions and vital signs
options.C: A detailed receipt of all community clinic registration fees
options.D: The patient's birth certificate and marriage license

explanation: A solid referral note tells the hospital team what you've done so far and why she's being sent. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h8)

question: Why must nurses follow strict legal boundaries when giving powerful medications?

options.A: Because the pharmacy department requires extra paperwork
options.B: Because these substances have a high risk of abuse and harm
options.C: To ensure that doctors do not prescribe any treatment
options.D: So that hospital management can monitor daily staffing

explanation: Strong medications carry serious risks like addiction or overdose, making strict rules necessary for patient safety. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h1)

question: Why is it important to talk about contraception early after birth, even before periods return?

options.A: Hormonal changes permanently stop ovulation for at least one year
options.B: Lactation guarantees complete protection against any future pregnancy
options.C: Menstruation always returns exactly six weeks after delivery
options.D: Fertility can return before the first postpartum menstrual period

explanation: Ovulation often happens before a mother sees her first period after birth. Knowing this helps us guide new mums safely! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h1)

question: Which of these is a natural, drug-free way to help a mum cope with labour pain?

options.A: Epidural anesthesia block
options.B: Intravenous opioid administration
options.C: Continuous back rubs and hydrotherapy
options.D: General surgical anesthesia

explanation: Massages, warm water (hydrotherapy), and breathing exercises work wonders for natural pain relief without medications. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h7)

question: Why is taking rifampicin (for TB) alongside certain HIV drugs tricky?

options.A: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in all patients
options.B: Rifampicin alters liver enzymes and can lower antiretroviral blood levels
options.C: Rifampicin stops the absorption of water in the stomach
options.D: The combination immediately destroys the patient's pancreas

explanation: You got it! Rifampicin speeds up liver enzymes so much that it can flush HIV drugs out of the blood too quickly, risking treatment failure. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T13#GNS215_U6_T13_h6)

question: What is the big difference between organ-specific and systemic autoimmune diseases?

options.A: Systemic conditions are caused exclusively by viral infections
options.B: Systemic diseases only affect the skin, while organ-specific affect the brain
options.C: Organ-specific conditions cannot be treated with medication
options.D: Organ-specific targets a single tissue, while systemic affects multiple organs

explanation: Organ-specific focuses its attack on just one place (like the thyroid), while systemic conditions cause widespread chaos across many parts of the body. [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h4)

question: Where should used injection needles be disposed of immediately after use?

options.A: A red biohazard bag for soft waste
options.B: A standard black plastic trash bag
options.C: A rigid, puncture-proof sharps container
options.D: The side pocket of the nurse's uniform

explanation: Puncture-proof sharps containers prevent accidental needle-stick injuries for nurses and housekeeping staff. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of applying a figure-eight elastic bandage to a residual limb after an amputation?

options.A: To permanently stop phantom limb pain
options.B: To replace the need for future prosthetic limbs
options.C: To increase blood flow to the surgical incision
options.D: To shape the stump and control swelling

explanation: Proper wrapping shrinks and shapes the residual limb so it can fit comfortably into a prosthetic socket later. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h5)

question: Why is hourly urine output a reliable way to monitor a patient in shock?

options.A: The bladder relaxes completely when blood pressure falls too low
options.B: Fluid intake must match output within a strict ten-minute window
options.C: Kidneys shut down urine production early to save fluid when perfusion drops
options.D: Urine turns dark because red blood cells break down rapidly

explanation: Because the kidneys receive lower priority during shunting, urine production drops quickly when overall perfusion is failing. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary clinical use for an intravenous dose of adenosine?

options.A: Terminating paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia
options.B: Thinning the blood to prevent sudden stroke events
options.C: Treating severe high blood pressure in the emergency room
options.D: Reversing a dangerous potassium overdose in the kidneys

explanation: Adenosine has a tiny half-life and is slammed fast intravenously to briefly stop AV node conduction and reset a fast rhythm. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why might a severely malnourished child fail to build strong protection after receiving a standard vaccine?

options.A: Malnutrition neutralizes the live virus inside the vaccine immediately
options.B: Undernourished children excrete all vaccine components through urine
options.C: The child's body temperature is too low for the vaccine to dissolve properly
options.D: Lack of essential nutrients prevents the body from building enough antibodies

explanation: Building antibodies takes raw materials like proteins and vitamins. If a child's nutrition is low, the body simply struggles to build that defense armor. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T70#GNS214_U1_T70_h2)

question: If you delegate a routine task to a nursing assistant as a registered nurse, who still holds the ultimate legal responsibility?

options.A: The hospital ward manager on duty
options.B: The nursing assistant who performed the task
options.C: The registered nurse who made the delegation
options.D: The physician in charge of the patient

explanation: Remember this rule: you can delegate tasks, but you can never delegate ultimate accountability. As the RN, you supervise and check the final outcome! [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of group dietary counselling?

options.A: Providing peer support and shared experiences among participants
options.B: Ensuring every person receives a completely custom calorie goal
options.C: Allowing the nurse to review private lab results for each person
options.D: Eliminating the need for any individualized medical assessment

explanation: Groups let patients learn from each other's success stories and daily challenges, which builds strong emotional encouragement. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h3)

question: Why is the PDSA cycle so helpful in Nigerian healthcare settings with limited resources?

options.A: It allows nurses to test low-cost workflow changes without needing massive budgets
options.B: It forces the federal government to build new hospitals in every rural town
options.C: It automatically provides millions of naira in foreign grants to the hospital
options.D: It prevents nurses from ever having to deal with power outages or shortages

explanation: Brilliant! You don't need a huge budget to improve care. PDSA helps us make smart, practical changes with what we already have. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h7)

question: Up to how many days after a pregnancy ends is a death still officially counted as maternal mortality?

options.A: Within 1 year
options.B: Within 6 months
options.C: Within 7 days
options.D: Within 42 days

explanation: You've got this! A maternal death is counted if it happens during pregnancy or up to 42 days (6 weeks) after delivery from pregnancy-related causes. Keep up the great revision! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h1)

question: Which health issue puts an HIV-positive patient into WHO Clinical Stage 4?

options.A: A normal CD4 count with no physical complaints
options.B: Kaposi sarcoma or severe opportunistic infections
options.C: Recurrent common colds and mild skin rashes
options.D: Persistent generalized swollen lymph nodes only

explanation: Spot on! Stage 4 involves severe illnesses and indicator conditions that mark advanced HIV disease (AIDS). [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h5)

question: How does a shortened fallopian tube typically affect how a fertilized egg travels to the uterus?

options.A: It causes rapid transit, leading to early entry into the uterus
options.B: It traps the embryo permanently in the isthmus
options.C: It reverses the muscular waves pushing it backward
options.D: It completely stops all ciliary movement in the tubal lining

explanation: Because there is less distance to travel, the fertilized egg rushes through too quickly and reaches the uterus before it is fully ready to implant. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h4)

question: What is an important food safety habit a nurse should teach families to prevent cross-contamination?

options.A: Reusing cooking oil indefinitely without filtering it
options.B: Keeping raw foods and cooked foods strictly separated
options.C: Washing all kitchen knives with cold water only
options.D: Storing all fresh vegetables inside closed plastic bags in the sun

explanation: Always keep raw meats away from ready-to-eat meals so harmful bacteria don't hitch a ride onto your food. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h8)

question: Why is data analysis a critical step before planning any healthcare intervention?

options.A: It allows nurses to guess which disease is causing trouble without proof
options.B: It turns raw numbers into clear insights so the real problems become visible
options.C: It ensures that all health funding goes directly into hospital building projects
options.D: It stops community members from expressing their personal opinions

explanation: Without analysis, data remains a confusing pile of numbers that cannot guide effective action. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h6)

question: A patient asks why the doctor adjusts their tiopronin dose using 24-hour urine collections. What is your best nursing response?

options.A: To find the exact dose that lowers your urine cystine enough to stop stones from forming
options.B: To check if your liver is completely immune to protein toxicity
options.C: To measure how much calcium your bones are losing while taking the drug
options.D: To ensure you are drinking the exact recommended liters of soda daily

explanation: We use 24-hour urine tests to find the sweet spot: enough medicine to keep cystine levels low and prevent stones, without taking more than necessary. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T4#GNS223_U8_T4_h4)

question: In an adult, where are new blood cells mostly made?

options.A: The outer layer of the spleen
options.B: The cortex of the kidneys
options.C: Yellow bone marrow
options.D: Red bone marrow

explanation: You nailed it! Red bone marrow found in flat bones and the ends of long bones is the busy factory floor where all new blood cells are born. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h5)

question: Your patient just returned to the ward after a modified radical mastectomy. What is a key nursing action to prevent lymphedema?

options.A: Encouraging heavy weightlifting with the affected arm to improve strength
options.B: Keeping the affected arm hanging low by the bedside all day long
options.C: Applying a tight tourniquet to the affected arm every morning for exercise
options.D: Instructing the patient to avoid blood pressure checks and injections on the affected arm

explanation: Protect that arm! No BP cuffs, no needles, and no IV lines on the surgery side to keep the lymph fluid flowing smoothly. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h7)

question: Why can unsafe formula feeding sometimes pose an even greater danger to an infant than HIV?

options.A: Contaminated water and dirty bottles cause fatal diarrhea and severe malnutrition
options.B: Commercial formula lacks basic calories needed for normal brain growth
options.C: Babies fed with formula develop immediate resistance to routine vaccines
options.D: Prepared formula breaks down the infant immune system faster than the virus

explanation: Where clean water isn't guaranteed, bad hygiene around formula bottles can cause severe tummy bugs that put a baby's life at serious risk. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T12#GNS216_U6_T12_h3)

question: Which everyday Nigerian kitchen item is a powerhouse source of Vitamin A?

options.A: Polished white rice
options.B: Red palm oil
options.C: Processed wheat flour
options.D: Refined white sugar

explanation: Well done! Unrefined red palm oil is loaded with beta-carotene, which our bodies turn straight into healthy Vitamin A. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T007#GNS227_U3_T007_h3)

question: What does the clinical term 'undetectable viral load' mean for a patient on ART?

options.A: The immune system has stopped producing white blood cells
options.B: The virus has completely disappeared from every organ in the body
options.C: The amount of HIV in the blood is too low for standard lab tests to measure
options.D: The patient no longer needs to take their daily medications

explanation: An undetectable viral load means the medication has successfully suppressed the virus so standard blood tests cannot find it. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is the main job of resuscitative equipment in the ward?

options.A: To provide routine daily patient hygiene care
options.B: To monitor long-term chronic wound healing
options.C: To manage sudden cardiac or respiratory arrest
options.D: To deliver oral medications during meals

explanation: You've got this! Resuscitative tools are kept ready specifically for emergencies when a patient stops breathing or their heart stops. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why must you strictly tell a patient who just had transsphenoidal surgery NOT to blow their nose?

options.A: It triggers terrible allergic reactions to the nasal packing materials.
options.B: It pushes air into the ear tubes and causes permanent deafness.
options.C: It increases pressure inside the head and can ruin the surgical seal.
options.D: It causes too much mucus to form and blocks the sinus completely.

explanation: Blowing your nose spikes intracranial pressure. That sudden pressure can pop the tissue patch the surgeon placed over the surgical site, causing cerebrospinal fluid to leak out. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T9#GNS222_U2_T9_h8)

question: What dangerous hazard is often associated with bulging food cans?

options.A: High vitamin C loss
options.B: Excessive iron content
options.C: Natural yeast fermentation
options.D: Botulinum toxins

explanation: A bulging can indicates gas production by bacteria, most notably the dangerous bacterium that causes botulism. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h4)

question: How do nitrate medications help stop chest pain?

options.A: By speeding up the electrical rhythm of the heart
options.B: By dilating blood vessels to reduce heart workload
options.C: By thickening the blood to improve clot formation
options.D: By increasing the heart rate to pump faster

explanation: Nitrates act like widening the road—they relax blood vessels so blood flows more easily, taking a huge load off the heart and easing the pain. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the most common local side effect of a topical skin medication?

options.A: Sudden kidney failure
options.B: Contact dermatitis and redness at the site
options.C: Complete hair loss on the scalp
options.D: Severe high blood pressure

explanation: Mild skin irritation, redness, or itching right where the cream was applied are the most common reactions to topical products. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T12#GNS215_U6_T12_h8)

question: How does a community health nurse use epidemiological thinking during a clinic shift?

options.A: By focusing strictly on the medical chart of the person in front of them
options.B: By ordering expensive scans for every patient with a headache
options.C: By looking for patterns and causes of illness in the local community
options.D: By diagnosing complex genetic disorders without lab tests

explanation: Exactly! Community health nurses connect the dots between individual illnesses and broader local trends to help everyone stay healthy. Great thinking! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h1)

question: What main process causes osmotic diarrhoea?

options.A: Rapid muscle contractions moving food too fast to digest
options.B: Unabsorbed particles staying in the gut and drawing water in
options.C: Bacterial toxins directly forcing salt and water secretion
options.D: Bleeding ulcers leaking protein and blood into the bowel

explanation: Osmotic means pulling water! When certain substances aren't absorbed in your gut, they act like a magnet, drawing water right along with them into your stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why do complex birth defects require a whole team of different specialists?

options.A: Surgeons aren't allowed to talk to parents alone
options.B: Special machines can only be run by top administrators
options.C: Hospital rules require ten doctors to sign off
options.D: The condition affects multiple body systems needing different expert skills

explanation: When a baby's heart, breathing, feeding, and movement are all involved, it takes a village of experts working together to give the best care! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h7)

question: Why is documenting vaccine administration in the child health card important?

options.A: It creates an accurate health record to guide future clinical care
options.B: It acts as a legal receipt for fees paid at the clinic counter
options.C: It proves to the government that the nurse worked a full shift
options.D: It prevents mothers from visiting any other health facility ever again

explanation: Clear documentation ensures subsequent providers know which doses were given and when the next ones are due. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h4)

question: Which stage in the Kubler-Ross model involves a person trying to make a deal with God to change an inevitable outcome?

options.A: Acceptance
options.B: Denial
options.C: Bargaining
options.D: Anger

explanation: Bargaining involves trying to negotiate a different outcome or postpone the inevitable loss. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h2)

question: A patient scheduled for a skin snip is very anxious about pain. What is your best first response?

options.A: Cancel the procedure immediately without consulting the doctor
options.B: Administer general anesthesia to keep the patient completely asleep
options.C: Explain the procedure steps and reassure them about local anesthetic use
options.D: Tell the patient that the procedure is entirely painless and quick

explanation: Great nursing judgement! Walking patients through the steps and letting them know local numbing will be used calms their nerves. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h2)

question: Why do some drugs need a much higher dose when swallowed as pills compared to being given through an injection?

options.A: Intravenous drugs take longer to dissolve than liquid syrups or crushed pills.
options.B: First-pass metabolism in the liver inactivates a large portion of the oral dose.
options.C: Oral tablets contain inactive fillers that block the active ingredient completely.
options.D: The stomach acid destroys all intravenous drugs before they enter the arm veins.

explanation: When you swallow a pill, it goes straight to the liver via the gut first. The liver breaks a lot of it down before it even reaches the rest of the body! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T1#GNS125_U5_T1_h6)

question: A patient tells you, 'Nurse, I just don't feel right.' Which response is the best example of a clarifying question?

options.A: Take this thermometer and check your temperature immediately.
options.B: Why did you wait so long before coming to the clinic?
options.C: Do you have a headache, fever, or stomach pain right now?
options.D: Can you tell me more about what 'not feeling right' feels like?

explanation: Brilliant! Asking them to describe a vague feeling helps you get clear, specific details instead of guessing. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h3)

question: A patient using axillary crutches complains of numbness and tingling in their fingers. What instruction should the nurse provide?

options.A: Switch immediately to using a standard four-wheeled walker
options.B: Adjust the crutches so they fit higher up in the armpit
options.C: Lean your upper body forward to relieve hand pressure
options.D: Support your body weight on your hands, not your armpits

question: What is the main idea behind efficiency in healthcare?

options.A: Increasing the total number of private hospitals in urban areas
options.B: Reducing the number of patients admitted to emergency wards
options.C: Maximizing health benefits using the fewest possible resources
options.D: Ensuring that all medical staff receive equal monthly salaries

explanation: Efficiency is all about making the most of what we have without wasting precious resources or money. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is another name commonly used for leprosy?

options.A: Bright's disease
options.B: Lyme disease
options.C: Hansen's disease
options.D: Koch's disease

question: What is the main difference between cleaning and sanitizing?

options.A: Cleaning uses chemicals, while sanitizing uses only plain water
options.B: Cleaning washes away visible dirt, while sanitizing brings germs down to a safe level
options.C: Cleaning kills bacteria, while sanitizing removes grease
options.D: Cleaning is done daily, while sanitizing is done once a year

explanation: Think of cleaning as washing away the physical mess (like grease and crumbs), while sanitizing uses heat or chemicals to knock out invisible germs. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h6)

question: Which major organ in the body is the main target for hepatotropic viruses?

options.A: The pancreas
options.B: The liver

options.D: The stomach

question: Your patient suddenly starts wheezing, struggling to breathe, and breaking out in hives right after an IV medication starts. What is your very first action?

options.D: Document the vital signs in the patient chart.

question: What is a common consequence of poor communication during the implementation phase?

options.D: Instant failure of government financial auditing systems

question: What is the very first thing a healthcare team must do after a serious adverse event?

options.A: Filing a formal police report against the hospital
options.B: Immediate stabilization and care of the patient
options.C: Notifying the international health organization
options.D: Calling a press conference to explain the mistake

explanation: The patient's safety and clinical stabilization always come first right after any unexpected event happens. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h6)

question: As a psychiatric nurse evaluating a patient's unusual symptom, what is the most important question to ask yourself?

options.A: How quickly can medication completely erase this behavior?
options.B: What is the exact medical billing code for this diagnosis?
options.C: Which family member caused the patient to act this way?
options.D: What purpose does this symptom serve for the patient?

explanation: Always look for the 'why.' Understanding what job the symptom is doing for the patient helps you uncover its protective or adaptive role. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which fetal position is required for a safe home delivery?

options.B: Breech presentation
options.C: Transverse lie
options.D: Oblique position

question: During a postpartum breast check, which sign strongly suggests the baby is not latching on correctly?

options.A: Prominent superficial veins
options.B: Bilateral breast symmetry
options.C: Cracked or bleeding nipples
options.D: Palpable lactiferous sinuses

question: If you notice stagnant water sitting outside a house, which part of the epidemiological triad does this represent?

options.A: The susceptible host factor

options.C: The environmental factor
options.D: The direct transmission factor

question: Which of these is a classic lung disease caused by breathing in mineral dust at work?

options.A: Cystic fibrosis
options.B: Silicosis
options.C: Acute bronchitis
options.D: Lobar pneumonia

explanation: Silicosis happens when workers breathe in tiny crystalline silica dust, often found in mining, construction, or masonry jobs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which child is at a higher risk for maltreatment?

options.A: Participating in community sports leagues
options.B: Excelling academically in primary school
options.C: Being the oldest child in a large family
options.D: Having a physical or developmental disability

explanation: Special needs require extra care, which can sometimes overwhelm stressed caregivers and increase vulnerability. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T24#GNS225_U5_T24_h3)

question: Which part of a homeostatic control system detects a change or stimulus in the environment?

options.A: Receptor
options.B: Control center
options.C: Set point
options.D: Effector

explanation: Receptors act as sensors that pick up changes in the environment and forward that data to the control center. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T10#GNS111_U1_T10_h2)

question: What are the two main components that make up the central nervous system?

options.A: Sensory receptors and motor organs
options.B: Nerves and ganglia
options.C: Sympathetic and parasympathetic systems
options.D: Brain and spinal cord

explanation: The central nervous system consists exclusively of the brain and the spinal cord, which serve as the primary processing center for the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the very first practical step when doing medication reconciliation during a home visit?

options.A: Calling the local pharmacy to order a fresh supply of all tablets
options.B: Gathering all current medication bottles and packages into one place
options.C: Asking the doctor to rewrite every prescription from the beginning
options.D: Throwing away any medicine that does not have a readable label

explanation: You got it! You have to round up all the medications first so you can actually see what the patient has and is taking. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of formative evaluation?

options.A: To give ongoing feedback to help you learn better
options.B: To check the school's financial budget
options.C: To pass the national licensing exam
options.D: To decide your final GPA for graduation

explanation: Formative evaluation is your friendly guide while you are still learning—it gives you feedback so you can improve before any big stakes exam. [learn more](GST321_U9_T2#GST321_U9_T2_h3)

question: What usually causes an infection control unit to launch an outbreak investigation?

options.A: A routine inspection of the hospital kitchen by local police
options.B: An unusual spike in infection numbers above the normal baseline
options.C: The purchase of new computers for the nursing station
options.D: The arrival of a single patient with a common seasonal cold

explanation: Correct! An outbreak is called when infections suddenly happen much more often than usual in a specific area. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h6)

question: Where should the top of a computer monitor be positioned relative to your eyes?

options.A: Far below chest height on the desktop
options.B: At or slightly below eye level
options.C: Turned sideways to your direct line of sight
options.D: Significantly higher than the top of the head

question: What is the main job of osteoclasts during the final bone remodeling phase?

options.A: Forming the primary blood clot in the gap

options.C: Pulling the broken bone ends back together
options.D: Creating the initial soft cartilage callus

question: What is the main problem happening in all types of shock?

options.B: Elevated blood sugar levels in the bloodstream
options.C: Sudden swelling of the upper respiratory tract
options.D: High fever caused by a bacterial infection

explanation: Simply put, shock means the body's tissues aren't getting enough blood and oxygen to survive and do their work. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h4)

question: When would a researcher use an inferential statistical test like a t-test?

options.A: To test hypotheses and compare group averages
options.B: To assign numerical codes to patient interview notes
options.C: To check paper survey forms for missing handwriting
options.D: To lock up digital files in a password-protected folder

explanation: Inferential statistics help you look beyond your immediate group to see if differences are significant enough to apply to a larger population. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h4)

question: How should public health nurses view addiction when counselling patients?

options.B: As a condition cured strictly by financial fines
options.C: As a complex health condition requiring support
options.D: As a minor habit that requires no intervention
